shell.notFoundBody: This address does not match anything in the console. The link may be outdated.

login.footerCaption: Registry console — sign in to continue
login.formSubtitle: Use the same credentials as docker login.
login.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Wait a minute, then try again.
login.serverError: The registry answered with an error ({{status}}). Try again in a moment.
login.unreachable: Could not reach the registry. Check your connection and try again.

overview.title: Overview
overview.subtitle: Images in this registry are addressed as
overview.noImagesBody: The first image pushed to this registry will appear here.
overview.pushBody: The commands below already contain this registry's address.
overview.recentActivityBody: Sign-ins, pushes, deletions and configuration changes.

images.title: Images
images.emptyBody: Push an image and its repository shows up here.
images.noMatchHint: Repositories are filtered by name. To find a specific tag, search all tags instead.
images.deleteBody_one: This removes the repository and its {{count}} tag. Storage is reclaimed by the next garbage collection. This cannot be undone.
images.deleteBody_other: This removes the repository and all {{count}} of its tags. Storage is reclaimed by the next garbage collection. This cannot be undone.

tagSearch.noMatchHint: The search covers repository names and tag names.

repository.compareHint: Select two tags to compare them.
repository.pickOneMore: {{tag}} selected — pick one more to compare.
repository.deleteTagBody: This removes the tag and the manifest it points to. Layers no other image uses are reclaimed by the next garbage collection.
repository.deleteTagSiblings: These tags point to the same manifest and will be removed too: {{tags}}
repository.missingBody: It may have been deleted, emptied by a retention policy, or never pushed to.
repository.pullBlockedHint: docker pull of this tag is refused by the vulnerability policy. Rebuild the image, or allowlist the CVEs on the Security page if the risk is accepted.

imageDetails.pullByDigestHint: Pulling by digest always gives exactly this image, even if the tag is moved later.
imageDetails.neverScanned: This image has not been scanned yet.
imageDetails.reusingScan: A recent scan of this exact image already exists — showing it.
imageDetails.browseLayer: Browse the files in this layer
imageDetails.historyBody: The instructions this image was built from, base first, with the layer each one added.
imageDetails.historyUnmatched: This image's layers can't be matched to its steps (it was squashed or rewritten), so sizes are not shown.
imageDetails.showMetadataSteps_one: Show {{count}} step that adds no layer
imageDetails.showMetadataSteps_other: Show {{count}} steps that add no layer
imageDetails.hideMetadataSteps: Hide steps that add no layer

layerBrowser.title: Layer contents
layerBrowser.empty: This layer adds no files — it only changes metadata.

tagDiff.layersSummary: Layers — {{shared}} shared, {{onlyACount}} only in {{tagA}}, {{onlyBCount}} only in {{tagB}}
tagDiff.identical: Both tags are built from exactly the same layers.

vulns.title: Vulnerability report
vulns.truncated: Showing the first {{shown}} of {{total}} — narrow the filters to see the rest.
vulns.cleanBody: Trivy found nothing in this image against its current vulnerability database.

activity.title: Activity
activity.description: Audit log of sign-ins, pushes, deletions and configuration changes. Entries cannot be edited from the console.
activity.emptyBody: Sign-ins, pushes and administrative actions are logged here as they happen.

storage.title: Storage
storage.description: What the registry stores, how it grows, and the rules that keep it in check.
storage.insightsFailed: Storage history could not be loaded.
storage.proxyTitle: Storage is managed by the upstream registry
storage.proxyBody: In proxy mode Dockyard keeps no blobs of its own, so there is nothing to size, collect or retain from here.

insights.largestBody: Size of the layers each repository references. Shared layers count once per repository.
insights.growthBody: Total stored size, sampled every 6 hours.
insights.notEnoughSamples: Not enough history yet — the first two samples are needed to draw a trend.

gc.title: Garbage collection
gc.description: Deleting a tag only removes the reference. Garbage collection is what frees the layers nothing points to any more. It also runs every night at 00:00 UTC.
gc.nothing: Nothing to collect — every blob is still referenced.
gc.skippedRecent_one: {{count}} unreferenced blob was left alone: it was uploaded in the last {{minutes}} minutes and may belong to a push still in progress.
gc.skippedRecent_other: {{count}} unreferenced blobs were left alone: they were uploaded in the last {{minutes}} minutes and may belong to a push still in progress.
gc.failedCount_one: {{count}} blob could not be deleted — check the server log.
gc.failedCount_other: {{count}} blobs could not be deleted — check the server log.
gc.nothingListed: The storage backend returned no blobs although repositories exist. Check its permissions (S3 needs s3:ListBucket).
gc.confirmBody: Every blob no manifest references is deleted permanently. Blobs uploaded recently are kept, so pushes in progress are safe.
gc.confirmForceBody: Every blob no manifest references is deleted permanently — including recently uploaded ones. A push that is in progress right now will be corrupted. Only continue if nobody is pushing.

retention.title: Retention policies
retention.description: Rules that delete old tags automatically, every night before garbage collection. The first policy whose pattern matches a repository applies to it.
retention.formIntro: A tag is deleted when it falls outside every rule below. Tags sharing a digest with a kept tag are never deleted.
retention.keepNHint: Number of tags to keep per repository. 0 turns this rule off.
retention.unpulledDaysHint: Days without a pull. 0 turns this rule off.
retention.protectedTagsHint: Exact tag names that are never deleted, comma-separated.
retention.needOneRule: Set at least one of the two rules above to create the policy.
retention.ruleUnpulled_one: delete after {{count}} day without a pull
retention.ruleUnpulled_other: delete after {{count}} days without a pull
retention.deletePolicyBody: The policy for {{pattern}} stops applying. Tags it already deleted are not restored.
retention.applyBody: Every tag the policies select is deleted immediately and cannot be restored. Preview first if you are unsure.
retention.applied_one: Retention applied — {{count}} tag deleted. Run garbage collection to free the space.
retention.applied_other: Retention applied — {{count}} tags deleted. Run garbage collection to free the space.
retention.nothing: No tag matches the policies — nothing to delete.
retention.emptyBody: Tags are kept forever until you delete them yourself.

quotas.title: Quotas
quotas.description: Caps on how much a repository or a user may push. Usage counts every byte pushed, before deduplication, and never decreases on its own — reset it after cleaning up.
quotas.warnAtHint: Sends a quota warning event once usage crosses this share of the limit.
quotas.resetBody: Usage for {{scope}} goes back to zero. The limit stays as it is.
quotas.emptyBody: Pushes are only limited by the space available.

security.title: Security
security.description: Known vulnerabilities in the images stored here, and which repositories require signed pushes.

scans.title: Vulnerability scans
scans.description: Latest scans across the registry. Start one from an image's details.
scans.emptyBody: Open an image and choose “Scan now” to check it against the Trivy vulnerability database.
scans.disabledSuffix: on the server and restart it to scan images with the bundled Trivy.

signing.title: Signed pushes
signing.description: When required, a tag can only be pushed if the image carries a valid cosign signature. Push by digest, sign, then push the tag.
signing.noKeysWarning: Signatures are required but no public key is configured, so every tag push to a gated repository is rejected. Set COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEYS_DIR on the server.
signing.noOverride: No per-repository override — the default applies everywhere.
signing.overrideIntro: Overrides the default for the repositories matching a pattern. The first matching override wins.
signing.deleteBody: Repositories matching {{pattern}} go back to the default.

access.title: Access
access.description: Who can sign in, what they can do, and where they are signed in from.
access.newUserIntro: The account works for the console and for docker login.
access.editIntro: Changes apply to the account's very next request.
access.roleHint_admin: Full access, including deleting images and managing users.
access.roleHint_pusher: Can pull and push images. Cannot delete or administer.
access.roleHint_reader: Can browse and pull images only.
access.repositoriesHint: Limit the account to these repositories — comma-separated, * as wildcard. Leave empty for all repositories.
access.newPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep the current one. Setting it signs the user out everywhere. At least {{min}} characters.
access.newPasswordSelfHint: Leave empty to keep your current password.
access.cannotDeleteSelf: You cannot delete your own account
access.deleteBody: The account loses access immediately — console, docker login and any open session. Audit entries are kept.
access.sessionsBody: Console and CLI sign-ins. Revoking one ends it immediately.
access.revokeBody: {{username}} is signed out of that device immediately and has to sign in again.
access.revokeSelfBody: This is the session you are using: you will be signed out immediately.

vulnPolicy.title: Vulnerability policy
vulnPolicy.description: Scan what gets pushed, and keep vulnerable images from being deployed.
vulnPolicy.scanningOff: Scanning is turned off (SCAN_ENABLED): nothing is scanned or blocked until it is on. The policy below is kept for when it is.
vulnPolicy.scanOnPushHint: Every pushed tag is queued for a scan as soon as it arrives.
vulnPolicy.blockPullsHint: docker pull is refused, with the CVEs listed, when the latest scan finds a vulnerability at this level that is not on the exceptions below. Images not scanned yet are not blocked.
vulnPolicy.allowlistBody: Vulnerabilities reviewed and accepted: they never block a pull, until the exception expires.
vulnPolicy.allowlistEmpty: No exception. Every vulnerability at or above the threshold blocks.
vulnPolicy.allowIntro: Use this when a vulnerability does not apply to how the image is used, or a fix is not available yet.
vulnPolicy.vulnerabilityHint: As listed in the scan report: CVE-…, GHSA-…
vulnPolicy.reasonHint: Why it is acceptable — shown to whoever reviews the exception later.
vulnPolicy.expiresHint: Re-assess it when it expires: from then on it blocks again.
vulnPolicy.removeBody: Images affected by it are blocked again from their next pull.
vulnPolicy.unavailableTitle: The vulnerability policy is not available

robots.title: Robot accounts
robots.description: Credentials for CI pipelines and clusters, instead of a person's password. They only work with docker login, cannot delete anything, and cannot open the console.
robots.newIntro: The secret is shown once, right after creation.
robots.name: Name
robots.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and . _ -. docker login username: {{username}}
robots.roleHint_reader: Can pull images only — for a cluster or a deployment environment.
robots.repositoriesHint: Limit the robot to these repositories — comma-separated, * as wildcard. Leave empty for all repositories.
robots.expiresHint: A secret that expires limits the damage if it leaks into a log.
robots.secretOnce: Copy it now, into your CI's secret store: it will never be shown again.
robots.rotateBody: The current secret stops working immediately: update the CI that uses it.
robots.deleteBody: Everything using this robot loses access to the registry on its next request.
robots.emptyBody: Create one per pipeline or cluster: each gets its own rights, and can be revoked without touching the others.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: Connect the registry to the rest of your tooling: notify other systems, and copy images to other registries.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.descriptionPrefix: HTTP calls sent when something happens in the registry, retried with backoff. With a secret, each payload is signed in the
webhooks.secretHint: Used to compute an HMAC of each payload.
webhooks.testFailed: The endpoint did not accept the test event
webhooks.deleteBody: {{url}} stops receiving events. Deliveries still queued for it are dropped.
webhooks.emptyBody: Add one to notify a chat channel or trigger a deployment when an image is pushed.

replication.title: Replication
replication.description: Each tag pushed here is copied to every enabled target whose pattern matches — layers and all platforms included. Copies are retried if the target is briefly unreachable.
replication.formIntro: The target must be a registry this server can reach and push to.
replication.name: Name
replication.patternHint: Only repositories matching this pattern are copied. * copies everything.
replication.unreachable: The target could not be reached
replication.deleteBody: Images are no longer copied to {{name}}. What was already copied stays there.
replication.emptyBody: Add one to keep a copy of your images in another registry.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Your account and how the console looks for you.
settings.cliBody: The same username and password work from Docker and from the dockyard-cli tool.
settings.sessionsBody: Everywhere your account is signed in. Signing a session out ends it immediately.
settings.signOutOthersBody_one: {{count}} other session will be ended right away. This one stays signed in.
settings.signOutOthersBody_other: {{count}} other sessions will be ended right away. This one stays signed in.
settings.signOutSessionBody: {{client}} will be signed out right away.
settings.serverConfigBody: How this instance is set up. Read-only: each value comes from the environment variable shown next to it (or the matching Helm value) and changes on restart.
